text: Can you see the Great Wall from space? Most astronauts say no.
The wall is long. More than twenty thousand kilometres, with all its branches.
But it is thin. Most of it is about as wide as a road.
And it is made of earth and stone, the same colours as the hills around it.
The Space Station flies four hundred kilometres up.
From there, seeing the wall is like spotting a pencil from four hundred metres away.
So astronauts almost never spot it with just their eyes.
What do they see? Cities, airports and highways, lit up at night.
The wall is huge. Just not from up there.
